streams.why_RELEASE_and_the_managers_reasoning_i: I offered the choice with a recommendation; his reasoning corrects a weaker version of mine and is recorded because it is the better argument. `dist` is embedded from the SAME bytes in both profiles, and the texts and the contrast the owner judges live in `dist` - so the SUBJECT of the acceptance does not depend on the profile at all, only the native half does. RELEASE therefore deletes the frames' standing caveat ('release untested') WITHOUT changing what the acceptance measures: a strict option with no cost in substance, the price being only a cold build's time. And his third point inverts my own counter-argument: if RELEASE ever diverges from DEBUG, that is a finding to obtain BEFORE the acceptance rather than something hidden by picking the profile that matches the pictures - exact agreement with what was expected proves almost nothing while feeling like proof.
streams.what_I_can_and_cannot_verify_about_the_e:
This replaces the manager's STOP as he wrote it, by his own instruction, because his version named a measurement that does not exist. THE INPUT is verifiable with certainty: `tauri.conf.json` declares `build.frontendDist = ../dist`, so the build reads that directory, and the driver pins dist/index.html to 96b6bd5000f957155569b342a236c17b51e244a8291475cf82260d1980fdf3fa both BEFORE and AFTER, since a build must not rewrite its own input. THE OUTPUT is NOT verifiable by inspecting the binary, and that is measured rather than assumed.

How it was measured, including the part where I was briefly fooled: I searched the existing 2026-09-30 release binary for one of the NEW texts and got 0, which agreed with expectation ('an old binary has no new strings') and would have been banked. The POSITIVE CONTROL destroyed it - a string that MUST be there, `Войдите в аккаунт Skipi`, also returned 0, proving the instrument blind rather than the binary old. Then I measured HOW blind: `strings` finds `<!DOCTYPE html` (5 hits) and `<title>` (4) but NOT `mobile-status`, NOT `loginRefusalText`, NOT `data-theme`, and ZERO Cyrillic anywhere - the 1,131,783-byte document is stored compressed. And no asset manifest with a digest is left under target/release/build/*/out (checked: that tree holds dependency codegen like named_entities.rs and bindgen.rs, nothing about frontend assets).

So the honest chain is: input proven by digest, output provable only by RUNNING the thing - which is the smoke stage, agreed as the next one.
streams.no_network_and_offline_is_what_makes_tha: `ports` is empty, and `--offline` is what earns it rather than hope. The shared registry cache holds 814 .crate files against 595 packages in the lock - but 814 >= 595 is a COUNT, not a composition, and it does not prove the right VERSIONS are present. I am not inferring from it. `--offline` makes cargo answer the question itself: if anything is missing it fails loudly, and that failure is returned as a finding rather than repaired by reaching for the network mid-stage. The registry cache is declared as a READ.
streams.the_window_floor_is_not_a_promise_of_fin: 240 s, which is nearly the whole window, and the reason is unusual: a cold release build of 595 packages will almost certainly OUTLAST any 300 s lease, and no floor can promise otherwise. So the floor does not mean 'enough time to finish' - it means 'start only at the BEGINNING of a window', so that an overrun is unambiguously an overrun rather than a near-miss. Per the standing rule the command is NOT interrupted on expiry: it is carried to the end and the stage closes with ack-stop from DRAIN_REQUIRED. Killing a build mid-flight would leave a partial target and there is no safe boundary inside it. The wall clock is recorded, and `overran_window=yes|no` goes into the record as a fact rather than an apology.
streams.the_positive_control_is_available_here_u: Stage 9 had to switch to a content-based control because stage 5's success had SPENT the 'absent -> exists' transition on FETCH_HEAD. Here the transition is available and unused: the vehicle carries no `src-tauri/target` at all, so the control is nothing -> a binary, with its digest, size and nanosecond mtime recorded. A second, independent half: the new binary must DIFFER from the 2026-09-30 house artefact, because two different commits cannot produce identical bytes - and that old digest is read LIVE rather than pinned as a constant, since a pinned prefix the script never compares would be a constant asserting something unchecked.
streams.release_sensitive_files_are_guarded_by_a: `Cargo.lock` and `Cargo.toml` are release-sensitive in this house and out of scope for a non-release task - they are exactly what blocked an earlier push. `--locked` makes cargo REFUSE rather than rewrite the lock, and that is a flag, i.e. a promise. So both digests are also compared after the build, and a change is a FINDING plus exit 22, not a note. The same treatment for dist/index.html: a build must not rewrite its own input.
streams.a_blind_spot_in_check_undefined_funcs_re: My first draft used `command -v cargo`, and the checker reported `command` as an undefined function: it reads a shell BUILTIN at statement start as a call. Isolated with minimal cases: `command -v ls` is flagged as `command`, `type -p ls` as `type`, while `export X=1` and `eval "f"` stay clean - so it is builtins MISSING FROM ITS ALLOWLIST, not builtins in general. Second instance of this family after the lowercase `case` patterns. I changed my side because a noisy reviewer instrument costs him a round, and the replacement is a better check anyway: `cargo --version` proves the toolchain RUNS rather than that a file sits on PATH. The blind spot goes to him separately rather than being papered over.
